story.text: The Budget was delivered on 28 October 2026. The OBR published its forecast the same day.
In March the OBR gave the Chancellor {march} of headroom against the stability rule in {year}.
Since then, higher interest on the debt took {debtInterest} of that away. Other changes gave back {other}.

sources.quote: Higher debt interest costs more than account for the change in borrowing and the reduction of headroom against the stability rule, in 2029‑30.

story.text: So before any measure the headroom was {before}. The measures added {measures}, leaving {headroom}.
The Budget document rounds that to £15 billion. The OBR calls it about half the margin Chancellors have kept since 2010.

sources.quote: There is a buffer of £15 billion against the stability rule and £24 billion against the investment rule.
The margin against the Government’s fiscal mandate of £15 billion is around half of the average margin that previous Chancellors have left against their fiscal mandate since 2010.

story.text: Both fiscal rules are met. The welfare cap is missed by {welfareGap}, after the OBR’s adjustments.

sources.quote: This results in the welfare cap being on course not to be met by £3 billion once the margin is included.

story.text: By {year} the tax measures bring in {tax} a year. The spending measures cost {spending}.

measures.plain: A £100 council tax rebate for homes in bands A to D from January 2027.

notMovable.reason: Paid this winter, before the first year you can change.

measures.plain: No VAT on domestic electricity from October 2026 to July 2027.
The 5p cut in fuel duty stays until July 2027. The rise with prices waits until then.
Single bus fares in England outside London capped at £2 for a year from January 2027.

notMovable.reason: The cap ends in January 2028; its later years are the energy department’s savings that pay for it.

measures.plain: Higher tax-free mileage rates for people who drive their own car for work.
A new parental allowance for fathers, partners and adopters from April 2029.
Carer’s Allowance is withdrawn bit by bit above the earnings limit from 2030-31.
Universal credit’s £2,500 surplus earnings threshold kept for one more year from April 2027.
More books for children under five.
Tariffs suspended on food, heating oil and fertiliser until 2027 or 2028.
The cash ISA limit stays at £20,000 from April 2027.
Pubs, social clubs and live music venues get 35% off business rates from April 2027.
Small shops, cafes, pubs and hotels get small business rate relief up to higher values.
High street business rates bills frozen in real terms for two years from April 2027.
The tax-free trading allowance rises from £1,000 to £3,000 from April 2027.
Tariffs suspended on 72 more products, and kept suspended on 361 others in 2027-28.
Climate change levy frozen for electricity and LPG. The gas rate rises with prices from April 2028.
Red diesel duty cut by 3.7p a litre until July 2027.
Small drinks producers get a bigger duty relief from February 2027.
Seed funding for mayors, and £1.5 billion of cheaper loans for mayoral authorities.
Mayoral authorities keep a share of business rates growth from April 2027.
Local apprenticeship services extended to every mayor.
Priority investments and local growth projects across the UK.
A pilot in Cambridge: a new way to pay for land, homes and roads from April 2027.
Money for strategic authorities to build the capacity for their new powers.
Founders’ Relief: 10% capital gains tax for founders of fast-growing companies from April 2027.
Simpler forms for claiming research and development tax reliefs from April 2027.
A bigger share option limit of £120,000 for the smallest growth companies from April 2027.
The British Business Bank invests £1 billion sooner and can lend £2 billion more.
The National Wealth Fund invests more, including £2 billion in a new Energy Wealth Fund.

notMovable.reason: What is scored is the running cost of lending, not the capital; the fund’s decisions are its own.

measures.plain: Money for AI security, for AI across the economy, and for UK AI capabilities.
Cheaper charging at local, lower-powered public chargers in Great Britain.
A route off the streets for rough sleepers, with housing and support afterwards.
Part of it paid for from the housing department’s existing budgets.
£1.5 billion more for around 10,000 social and affordable homes.
No VAT on land sold to social housing providers from April 2027.
Your First Home: an equity loan for around 70,000 first-time buyers from April 2027.

notMovable.reason: What is scored is the fee income from developers; the loans are capital the Treasury lends and gets back.

measures.plain: A First Time Buyer ISA replaces the Lifetime ISA for new savers from April 2029.
Lifetime ISA savers buying a home above the £450,000 cap pay a 20% charge, not 25%.
Spending on the Defence Investment Plan beyond the savings promised in June 2026.

notMovable.reason: The plan’s own spending; how it is paid for is line 41.

measures.plain: Capital moved from other departments to fully fund the Defence Investment Plan.
Defence’s back-office savings go to the front line and national security.
Emergency winter support for Ukraine’s air defence.
UK Export Finance backs more defence exports. The fees come in from June 2026.

notMovable.reason: Income from activity already under way.

measures.plain: More HMRC staff and powers to collect tax that goes unpaid.
Online marketplaces collect the VAT on sales by UK sellers from October 2027.
The DWP uses more data and checks to stop fraud and error entering the benefits system.
Serious offenders held in hospital lose benefit entitlements from April 2027.
The rules on taking money out of a company are tightened from April 2028.
Advance corporation tax is abolished from April 2031.
A VAT rule on services bought from overseas is narrowed from April 2027.
Pensioners with no more income than the state pension pay no income tax. It runs from 2027 to 2030.
The two-year rule on taxing pension death benefits goes from October 2026.
Foreign states investing in UK property pay tax on it from January 2029.
The bank surcharge doubles to 6% for fifteen months from January 2027.
Duty on higher-stake gaming machines rises from 20% to 25% from April 2027.
Vape shops and adult gaming centres lose business rates reliefs from April 2027.
Firms write off plant and machinery more slowly. The main allowance falls from 14% to 12%.
The biggest taxi and private hire apps pay VAT on the whole fare from January 2028.
Business asset disposal relief is capped at £500,000 of gains from April 2027.
Two points more income tax on rental income from April 2027.
Two points more income tax on savings interest from April 2027.
Departments cut their running costs by 20% by 2029-30, not the 16% planned.
Part of that saving funds an AI programme to cut paperwork in government.
Vehicle excise duty on lorries cut to £1 for a year from July 2026.

notMovable.reason: Over before the first year you can change.

measures.plain: VAT on family days out cut to 5% for summer 2026.

notMovable.reason: Over before the first year you can change.

measures.plain: Free bus travel for children aged 5 to 15 in England in August 2026.

notMovable.reason: Over before the first year you can change.

measures.plain: Foreign branches of UK companies are exempt from UK tax. Their losses no longer cut it.
The electricity generator levy rises from 45% to 55% until March 2028.
The industrial electricity scheme cuts bills for energy-intensive firms from April 2027.
Carbon price support ends from April 2028 to cut energy bills.
A bigger Youth Guarantee and more apprenticeship support.
The Union Learning Fund is set up again in England.
Investment for growth: strategic technologies, local growth and key industries.
The Growth Guarantee Scheme backs £6.5 billion more lending to smaller firms.
Leeds keeps all the growth in its business rates.
The trade deal with India comes into force from July 2026.
Tariffs and quotas on imported steel change from July 2026.
A Securities Transfer Tax replaces stamp duty on shares from late 2027.
No business rates on electric vehicle charging points for ten years.
Grassroots programmes to prevent misogyny.
Infected blood compensation follows the Inquiry’s further recommendations.
Interest on Plan 2 and Plan 3 student loans capped at 6% for a year from September 2026.
Landfill tax costs covered for clearing six illegal waste sites, and a pilot for councils.
Money for key pressures, including the NHS and the plan on violence against women and girls.
Company car tax rates set for 2030-31.

notMovable.reason: Rates for a year beyond the target year.

measures.plain: A licensing regime for supported housing from 2027-28.
No VAT on donated medicines from June 2026.
VAT on temporary medical staff restored to what the law intended.

notMovable.reason: A correction to what the law intended.

measures.plain: Landfill operators can give more to community funds from April 2027.
Franchised university providers with 300 or more students must register from September 2028.
Council budgets for special educational needs adjust for pay and teachers’ pensions.
Who can defer or be let off the high value council tax surcharge, from April 2028.
Payrolling of company car and medical benefits waits until April 2027, the rest until April 2028.
The £135 customs duty relief on low value imports ends from October 2028.

notMovable.reason: Scored at nothing in the years you can change.

measures.plain: Waste incinerators join the emissions trading scheme later than planned.
Gas distribution firms spread a one-off change in their accounts over five years.
UK investors in US limited liability companies no longer pay tax twice from early 2028.

themes.title: Your income and savings
themes.lead: Tax on what people earn on the side, save, rent out and draw as a pension.

cards.title: Savings interest taxed two points more
cards.explain: From April 2027, savings interest above your tax-free allowances is taxed two points more, at every rate. Interest in an ISA stays tax-free.

cards.title: Rent taxed two points more
cards.explain: From April 2027, landlords pay two points more income tax on the rent they get, at every rate.

cards.title: No income tax on the state pension alone
cards.explain: From 2027 to 2030, a pensioner who has only the new state pension pays no income tax on it. Above that, the help tapers away.

cards.title: £3,000 of side income tax-free
cards.explain: From April 2027, the first £3,000 a year from small trading and side jobs is tax-free, up from £1,000.

cards.title: More tax-free mileage for driving for work
cards.explain: If you drive your own car for work, your employer can pay 55p a mile tax-free for 10,000 miles. Above that, the rate rises to 35p from April 2027.

cards.title: The cash ISA limit stays at £20,000
cards.explain: You can still save up to £20,000 a year in a cash ISA from April 2027. A cut had been talked about.

themes.title: Businesses and investors
themes.lead: What companies pay, and what owners pay when they sell up or take money out.

cards.title: Firms write off machinery more slowly
cards.explain: From April 2027, firms deduct 12% of the value of their plant and machinery each year, not 14%. The first-year allowance rises from 40% to 50%.

cards.title: Foreign branch losses no longer cut UK tax
cards.explain: From January 2027, a UK company’s foreign branches are all outside UK corporation tax. Their profits are not taxed here, and their losses no longer cut the UK bill.

cards.title: Tighter rules on taking money out of a company
cards.explain: From April 2028, profits taken out of a company as capital are taxed as dividends where that is fairer.

cards.title: Founders’ Relief: 10% tax on company gains
cards.explain: From April 2027, founders and early investors in fast-growing companies pay 10% capital gains tax. It covers up to £10 million of gains.

cards.title: Less relief when you sell your business
cards.explain: From April 2027, the lower tax rate when you sell your business covers £500,000 of gains, not £1 million. Gains above that pay the main rates.

cards.title: Business rates help for the high street
cards.explain: From April 2027, pubs, clubs and music venues get 35% off business rates. Small shops, cafes and hotels get more small business relief. High street bills are frozen in real terms for two years.

themes.title: Collecting more tax
themes.lead: Collecting tax that goes unpaid, and new or higher taxes on banks, platforms and gaming machines.

cards.title: More HMRC staff to collect unpaid tax
cards.explain: The Budget pays for 670 more HMRC compliance officers and more debt collection. HMRC can also take small debts from the bank accounts of people who can pay but will not.

cards.title: Foreign states pay tax on UK property
cards.explain: From January 2029, foreign governments that invest in UK property pay tax on the income and the gains.

cards.title: Online marketplaces collect sellers’ VAT
cards.explain: From October 2027, online marketplaces collect the VAT on sales by UK sellers whose sales on the site pass £90,000.

cards.title: Taxi apps pay VAT on the whole fare
cards.explain: From January 2028, the biggest private hire firms pay VAT on the whole fare, not just their commission. It applies to firms with fares over £50 million a year.

cards.title: A bigger bank surcharge for 15 months
cards.explain: From January 2027 to March 2028, the extra tax on bank profits doubles from 3% to 6%. It helps pay for the Budget’s help with bills.

cards.title: Higher duty on gaming machines
cards.explain: Duty on higher-stake gaming machines rises from 20% to 25% from April 2027.

themes.title: Energy and fuel
themes.lead: Help with energy bills and fuel, and when waste burning starts paying for its carbon.

cards.title: No VAT on electricity until July 2027
cards.explain: Household electricity carries no VAT from October 2026 to July 2027. Then the usual 5% comes back.

cards.title: The fuel duty cut lasts until July 2027
cards.explain: The 5p cut in fuel duty lasts until July 2027. Then rates go up by 5p and with prices.

cards.title: Waste burners pay for carbon later
cards.explain: Waste incinerators join the UK Emissions Trading Scheme later than planned. Until they join, they buy no carbon permits.

cards.title: Cheaper electricity for heavy industry
cards.explain: From April 2027, the British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme cuts electricity bills for firms that use a lot of energy.

themes.title: Defence and government
themes.lead: How defence is paid for, what Whitehall saves, and what it spends more on.

cards.title: Capital moved to defence from other departments
cards.explain: The rest of the Defence Investment Plan is paid for by moving capital from other departments. Their capital budgets fall by 1% from 2027-28.

cards.title: A deeper cut to Whitehall’s running costs
cards.explain: Departments cut their administration budgets by 20% by 2029-30, not the 16% planned.

cards.title: Money for AI
cards.explain: The Budget spends on AI security, on using AI across the economy, and on the UK’s own AI capabilities.

cards.title: More checks on benefit fraud and error
cards.explain: The DWP uses more data and checks to stop fraud and mistakes getting into benefits, such as time spent abroad. It costs money at first and saves later.

cards.title: Big franchised colleges must register
cards.explain: From September 2028, franchised university providers with 300 or more students must register with the Office for Students. Otherwise their students cannot get loans.

themes.title: Homes and growth
themes.lead: Homes, help for rough sleepers and first-time buyers, and money for growth.

cards.title: About 10,000 more social homes
cards.explain: The Budget adds to the Social and Affordable Homes Programme, for around 10,000 more homes. Most will be for social rent.

cards.title: A route off the streets for rough sleepers
cards.explain: Rough sleepers in England get a route off the streets to 2028-29, with housing and support after. Part is paid for from existing housing budgets.

cards.title: A First Time Buyer ISA replaces the Lifetime ISA
cards.explain: From April 2029, new savers get a First Time Buyer ISA instead of a Lifetime ISA. It pays a 25% bonus towards a first home costing up to £450,000.

cards.title: Investment for growth
cards.explain: Money for new technologies, local growth and key industries.

cards.title: More state-backed loans for small firms
cards.explain: The Growth Guarantee Scheme backs more lending to smaller firms, with longer loans.
